DOESACANONICALORDERINGCLOSEITWITHOUTDELI.THEANSWERISNO_ANDHEREISWHY: A CANONICAL ORDERING DOES NOT CLOSE THIS WITHOUT DELIVERY'S AUTHORITY. It is the SAME FUNCTION -- it reproduces all four published digests exactly -- and therefore it inherits the same open question rather than answering it. A canonical ordering is well defined and provably idempotent, and it makes the injectivity statement true as an equation, which is the repair this artifact makes. But the sentence 'canonical(x) and x are the same logical value' IS the set ruling, restated. If provider order carries meaning, canonicalisation is a LOSSY normalisation and the two documents above are still two logical values on one id; if it does not, canonicalisation is information-preserving and the id is right. NOTHING IN THE ARITHMETIC DECIDES WHICH, AND THAT IS THE POINT. Relocating the claim from 'injective' to 'injective on canonical forms' is honest and is done here. Relocating the DECISION from DELIVERY to a canonicalisation rule would be law 19's forbidden act wearing a different word.
DOESACANONICALORDERINGCLOSEITWITHOUTDELI.whatACANONICALORDERINGDOESBUY: one thing, and it is worth saying because it is the only part a candidate can settle alone: it makes the failure LOUD instead of silent. Under a stated canonical ordering an implementer knows a normalisation happened and can ask whether it should have. Under v1's unqualified injectivity claim the same implementer was told no normalisation was possible. THAT is the difference the repair makes, and it is a difference in what a reader is told, not in what the bytes do.

whatAnImplementerHashesAndWHEN.where: inside evaluate, in the pure core. Not in the host, not in a port, not after return.
order: 1. run the rule stage under the budget rules; obtain findings (or partialFindings) and the final ExactCoverage, including any first-failed-charge rewrite to budget-exhausted. Determine variant and, if incomplete, deficiency.
2. build PolicyDerivationInputV1 from the arguments and those values. It contains no value produced by the policy stage.
3. derivationDigest = commit(record). ONE SHA-256 over the leaf, one over the outer frame.
4. run the policy stage; obtain verdict.
5. assemble PolicyOutcome { policyId: deps.policy.policyId, verdict, derivationDigest }.
whatAnImplementerHashesAndWHEN.noCycle: the record contains findings and exactCoverage, which are SIBLINGS of policyOutcome inside CoreCompletion, never policyOutcome itself. There is no self-reference and no fixpoint. EP8's VerdictInputV2 has the same property and for the same reason: its own derivationCommitment is carried in the value and excluded from the preimage.
whatAnImplementerHashesAndWHEN.theExhaustionPath: when the first failed charge ends evaluation, localEvaluationState.counters.exhaustion requires an incomplete completion with deficiency budget-exhausted and an INDETERMINATE policyOutcome. The policy stage did not run. derivationDigest is still computed, over the same record, and it still says what the policy WOULD have derived from -- which is why PDD-2 and PDD-3 differ: R1V15-POS-04 exhausts coverage:rule and R1V15-POS-05 exhausts coverage:policy, so their ExactCoverage differs.
whatAnImplementerHashesAndWHEN.cancelledAndFaulted: CoreCompletion::cancelled and ::faulted carry no policyOutcome, so no derivationDigest is computed on those paths. R-B has no encoding for them and the encoder refuses one (vector REJ-9). Confirmed against evidenceIdentity.projectionByVariant, which places policyOutcome in the completed and incomplete projections only -- .cancelled is [variant, exactCoverage] and .faulted is [variant, faultCause].

entries.statement: R-B excludes it, on the stated ground that 'derivation' is not 'outcome'. v1 filed this as 'OPEN -- REVIEWER MUST DECIDE' and said 'No artifact says either way'. THAT WAS OVER-DECLARED.

The same is true of that record's own `derivationCommitment`, and of coverage.projectId and policy.projectId: FOUR carried keys sit outside the preimage.

The right moment is the DELIVERY successor that rules on DUD-7, and the checker should be retained by whoever states the ruling. This is a JUDGEMENT and a reviewer may overrule it; it is recorded rather than presented as an oversight.

entries.title: Whether a capability manifest's four array positions are SETS or SEQUENCES. THE ORDERING DECISION DECIDES THE ID.
entries.statement: no artifact in this corpus states whether CapabilityManifestV1.providers, CapabilityManifestV1.coverageForAbsent, ProviderCapability.platformIds or AbsentCapability.relationIds is order-significant, and none states a uniqueness rule for any of them. delivery.v2#capabilityManifestSchema declares them as required members and says nothing more. JSON's own reading of an array is a sequence.
entries.whyITISHERERATHERTHANINknownLimitations: THIS IS THE REPAIR OF BLOCKER B-PPIR-01. v1 filed this choice as knownLimitations item 6 while filing an equally open choice (DUD-3) as a declaredUnresolvedDependency, and stated its injectivity proof unconditionally above it. The choice is MORE load-bearing than DUD-3, not less: it is what rescues or falsifies the injectivity claim, and it changes every published CAP digest.
entries.whyTHISARTIFACTMAYNOTDECIDEIT: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 6 law 19. The capability manifest is DELIVERY's object and whether its provider list carries meaning in its order is a fact about DELIVERY's data model.
entries.andACANONICALORDERINGDOESNOTAVOIDIT: measured, not assumed. A canonical ordering applied in the JSON domain reproduces all four published digests EXACTLY and is provably idempotent -- and canonical(documentA) equals canonical(documentB) for the reproduced collision, so it is the same function by another route. It makes the injectivity statement true as an equation and leaves the question 'is canonicalisation information-preserving' exactly where it was. See orderingDependency.DOESACANONICALORDERINGCLOSEITWITHOUTDELIVERYSAUTHORITY.
entries.bothReadingsArePUBLISHEDWithDigests: orderingDependency.WHATCHANGESUNDEREACHREADING_WITHCOMPUTEDDIGESTS carries every CAP id, record sha256, record byte length and outer preimage hex under BOTH readings, plus CAP-REV and all three derived PlanIds. Choosing is a one-line ruling with a fully computed cost.
entries.whatASUCCESSORMustDo: state, in DELIVERY's own bytes, whether each of the four positions is order-significant, and state a uniqueness rule alongside.

declaredUnresolvedDependencies.overall: SEVEN declared, ZERO closed by this artifact. DUD-1 is adjudicated by law 19 and its residue -- whether these are the right strings -- is DELIVERY's and R-1's. DUD-3 is downgraded on measured evidence. DUD-5, DUD-6 and DUD-7 are jointly why this file is NOT-APPLIED: no checker, no custody path, and an undetermined ordering. DUD-2, DUD-4, DUD-6 and DUD-7 are all preconditions on a successor rather than defects here.
